services/balcony-waterproofing/index.htm:
Does water pooling on a balcony mean the membrane has failed?

No. Ponding describes water remaining on the surface; it does not establish where a leak starts. Drainage outlets, surface falls, thresholds and waterproofing junctions may need assessment together. Tell us where water collects, how long it remains after rain and whether staining appears below. A drainage issue and a waterproofing defect can require different work, even when both symptoms occur.

The balcony leak guide explains why the visible stain may not identify the entry point. Where access to the waterproofing layer is needed, ask the written scope to distinguish tile removal, substrate work, membrane details and retiling from any separate drainage work.

What should I give the strata manager if the unit below is affected?

Share the dates and weather conditions, the affected locations above and below, any safely taken photographs and records of previous repairs. Identify who can arrange access to each area and ask what approval is required before an inspection or work begins. These records support the discussion; they do not establish responsibility for the defect or its cost. Contact MEL ONE about the balcony with the available information and any access or approval constraints so the proposed assessment can be discussed.
services/bathroom-waterproofing/index.ht:
Can just the shower be waterproofed and retiled?

Sometimes a shower-only scope is feasible. The decision depends on the substrate, adjoining waterproofing details and how the repaired area can connect to the surrounding construction. Explain which fittings and finishes you want to retain so the assessment can establish the required access. A local scope still needs to address the affected waterproofing system.

What if I have already bought tiles for my ensuite?

Send the tile specifications, sizes and available quantity when discussing the work. Suitability, layout, substrate condition and compatibility with the proposed installation need review before owner-supplied materials can be included. Ask the quote to identify who supplies tiles and other materials, and what happens if additional preparation or tiles are needed.

How should work be planned when we have only one bathroom?

Tell MEL ONE before agreeing the scope. Ask which facilities will be unavailable and when access can resume, allowing for preparation, membrane and finishing requirements. The actual system and site conditions determine the sequence; arrange alternative washing facilities around the confirmed plan. Use the waterproofing and retiling quote guide to request separate removal, substrate, membrane, tiling, finishing and waste-removal items, then discuss your bathroom requirements.
services/external-waterproofing/index.ht:
What should be checked when a window leaks in wind-driven rain?

The window joints, frame drainage and surrounding wall details may all be relevant. Tell us which side gets wet first and whether the problem occurs only with a particular wind direction. Water visible beside the frame can originate elsewhere, so the symptom alone does not justify sealing every opening or coating the wall. Dampness that also appears without rain may need a different investigation.

Does rainwater under a back door need more silicone?

Not necessarily. The threshold, adjoining joints, outside surface levels and drainage need consideration. Describe whether water reaches the doorway as surface runoff or appears through a particular gap. A local seal is useful only where it addresses an identified joint defect; threshold or drainage work may need a separate scope.

What if water pools against the side wall?

Ask for drainage and surface falls to be considered alongside any water-entry detail. A coating alone may leave the source of pooled water unresolved. The waterproofing or drainage guide helps frame the discussion. For water appearing at the eaves, start with the roof leak service. Otherwise, report the rain pattern and affected area so the appropriate assessment can be discussed.
services/kitchen-sealing/index.html:
Is water under the sink coming from the edge or a pipe?

It can come from either, so the location of a wet cupboard is only a starting point. Water appearing after splashes on the benchtop may point towards a sink-edge joint. Water appearing around a tap connection, trap or waste pipe needs plumbing assessment. Describe when the cupboard gets wet and where you first notice water without dismantling connections to investigate.

If an accessible sink perimeter or splashback-to-benchtop joint is the confirmed issue, the sealing scope can identify the old sealant to remove, the surfaces to prepare and the joints to reseal. The sink resealing or plumbing guide helps explain which details to report.

Will resealing restore a swollen kitchen cabinet?

No. Resealing a confirmed joint leak addresses that water path; it does not restore a swollen or softened cabinet board. Find and address the moisture source before planning replacement or other cabinet repairs. Ask whether damage around the joint affects the sealing work, and have any cabinet restoration identified separately. Describe the sink, cupboard and timing to discuss the appropriate assessment. A kitchen sealing quote should specify its actual junction repairs rather than assume the same scope as a bathroom renovation.
services/laundry-waterproofing/index.htm:
What should I arrange before the laundry tiler starts?

Arrange assessment before new tiles cover the floor and junctions. Tell MEL ONE whether old tiles remain, what preparation is already complete and who is handling tiling and appliance connections. Share the proposed tile finish and any changes to the floor waste or doorway so the waterproofing scope can be reviewed against the planned layout.

Agree who prepares the substrate, who confirms it is ready for the next stage and how the selected membrane's curing requirements affect the tiling sequence. Confirm appliance disconnection and reconnection separately with the responsible trade. Use the quote guide to prepare questions, then discuss the laundry before booking the next stage.
services/leaking-shower-repairs/index.ht:
What if carpet, paint or the ceiling gets wet after a shower?

Wet carpet beside the shower, bubbling paint on the wall behind it or a ceiling drip after an upstairs shower are reasons to arrange an assessment. These signs alone do not identify a failed membrane. Water may escape through a screen edge or junction, or come from a supply or waste connection. A plumbing fault needs a plumber; a waterproofing repair should follow the assessed water path.

Tell us where the first moisture appears, whether it follows every shower and whether it also occurs when the shower is unused. Existing photos and a description of earlier repairs can help. Our shower plumbing or waterproofing guide explains the different repair paths.

Why is the shower still leaking after regrouting or resealing?

A surface repair may not have addressed the source, or another detail may need attention. Before paying for more grout or silicone, describe what was repaired and whether the symptom changed. The assessment can then consider those details and whether access beneath finishes is needed. Bathroom waterproofing and retiling is the route for an agreed membrane renewal scope; contact MEL ONE if the cause is still unclear.
services/roof-waterproofing/index.html:
What should I report if water comes from the eaves?

Describe where it appears, whether gutters visibly overflow and whether a ceiling or wall inside is also affected. Eaves dripping during rain can involve roof or gutter details; the observation does not identify a membrane defect. Report what you can see from a safe position on the ground and let the assessment determine any access needed.

What information helps with a leak at a roof-to-wall junction?

Note the affected room, the weather when the leak starts and any previous flashing or roof repairs. Existing plans or photographs can help describe the roof construction. Ask the proposed scope to identify the affected junction and any separate roofing or drainage task before choosing a treatment. Discuss the roof leak with MEL ONE; if water instead appears around a window or doorway, see external water ingress repairs.
services/shower-resealing-regrouting/ind:
Does water escaping at the shower screen need resealing?

A local screen-perimeter repair may be suitable if assessment identifies an accessible failed joint as the water path. Tell us whether water first appears at the screen base, beside the door or outside a tiled corner. The screen arrangement and its drainage details need consideration before deciding which joints should be sealed. Adding silicone wherever water is visible can miss the actual entry point.

Why does old silicone need attention before new sealant is applied?

The condition of the joint and its bonding surfaces matters. The agreed repair should identify the failed material to remove and the preparation needed for the replacement sealant. Loose grout, damaged tiles or movement may change the scope. Ask which screen edges or tiled junctions are included and which surrounding surfaces will be retained.

Can silicone repair a concealed waterproofing membrane?

Silicone is a joint sealant; it does not replace the membrane beneath tiled finishes. If moisture continues beyond the shower or returns after a surface repair, use the leaking shower assessment service to review the cause. The repair options guide explains when grout, sealant or broader waterproofing work may be relevant. Describe the affected joints before choosing a repair.
